paragraphs: Friend, look at where this prayer starts. The Levites don't open with the mess. They open with who God is: "You alone are the LORD." (Nehemiah 9:6) Confession that skips straight to the failures is just a bad day on replay, but confession that starts with God knows exactly who is listening.

Then the prayer gets honest, painfully honest. Israel's fathers rebel, cry out, get delivered, and do it all over again, and the Levites say every bit of it out loud. Yet the answer keeps coming back to God, because He is "a gracious and compassionate God." (Nehemiah 9:31) I'm in no position to judge anybody's cycle, since I once swore to stop scorching the bottoms of my cookies and the smoke alarm laughed at me.

And the prayer doesn't stop at feeling bad. The Levites say God has been just, "while we have acted wickedly," (Nehemiah 9:33) and then the people make a binding agreement in writing (Nehemiah 9:38). So here's the lesson for you, baker: tell God the truth, remember His compassion, then take a real step. This story isn't over, either.
